title: Cobalt: seabed nodules vs all land-based reserves (million tonnes)

source.name: Clarion-Clipperton Zone resource assessment vs global land reserves
source.publisher: International Seabed Authority (seabed figure) / U.S. Geological Survey Mineral Commodity Summaries (land figure)

notes: ISA-cited figures put the Clarion-Clipperton Zone's polymetallic nodules at roughly 44 million tonnes of contained cobalt (also ~270 million tonnes of nickel and ~6 billion tonnes of manganese) -- more of each metal than is known on land. USGS's 2024 Mineral Commodity Summary put total global land-based cobalt reserves at about 11 million tonnes, over half of it in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
